headline: UPDATE (extends 1400-02/1500-03/1600-03)
dek: Egypt's parliament on Sunday postponed the vote on President Sisi's request to authorize military support for Saudi Arabia against Ansar Allah attacks, extending deliberations into Monday (Egyptian media say into Tuesday). The ~3-hour closed session ended with no vote.
sources: Agence France-Presse (two lawmakers: Ibrahim Kholeif, Maha Abdel Nasser); Mada Masr (three MPs); South24 Center
fault_line: Should Egypt put its soldiers on the line for Saudi Arabia — pan-Arab defense against Ansar Allah strikes, or is Sisi renting the Egyptian army for Gulf money while Gaza bleeds?

sections.what_happened: Egypt's parliament on Sunday postponed the vote on President Sisi's request to authorize military support for Saudi Arabia against Ansar Allah attacks, extending deliberations into Monday (Egyptian media say into Tuesday). The ~3-hour closed session ended with no vote. MP Ibrahim Kholeif told AFP the extension was 'to give all lawmakers the opportunity to speak and express their views', adding parliamentarians were mostly in support. No details were discussed of what form Egypt's support would take. As of Sunday, no formal Saudi request related to the authorization had been announced. Background: NDC (chaired by Sisi) had earlier Sunday approved supplying Saudi Arabia with 'all necessary and available forms of support' to defend territory and holy sites. Article 152 of Egypt's constitution requires two-thirds House approval for sending forces abroad on a combat mission.
sections.what_verified: AFP wire carried by Business Recorder, Kuwait Times, Türkiye Today, Gulf News, The News (Pakistan), newscentraltv (Asharq Al-Awsat credit); independent confirmation via Mada Masr (closed session ran ~3 hours, vote put off until after Monday/Tuesday sessions, MPs barred from sharing details) and South24 (Article 152 two-thirds bar).
sections.what_disputed: Sisi framed the request as defensive only ('We are speaking only in defense'), appealed for an end to fighting, and NDC statement paired support with continued political/diplomatic efforts. Supporters argue Saudi-funded aid to Egypt (billions since 2013) makes defense reciprocal. Ansar Allah parliament speaker Yahya al-Rai warned Cairo intervention would be 'a grave danger' to Egypt's own security — leverage for the delay narrative.
sections.why_matters: Cairo hesitates: the Arab world's largest army pauses on the Saudi rescue vote while Riyadh takes near-daily Ansar Allah fire — air defenses strained, Kingdom Centre on mandatory remote work. Side-of-truth framing: Egypt's constitutional bar (two-thirds) and MPs demanding details is due process, not disloyalty; note who else is circling the same day — Macron's Gulf tour (Barrot in Riyadh Sunday evening) and Lavrov in Tehran Monday. Carry Sisi's own words ('only in defense') and al-Rai's warning with source tags.
